problems.title: Order trigonometric values
problems.question: Order a=tan243°, b=sin90°, c=tan223° decreasingly.
problems.idea: Use trigonometric identities and a perpendicular-section or vector model for spatial geometry.
formulas: a=tan63°, b=1, c=tan43°. Tangent increases on(0°,90°).
steps: Since 43°<45°<63°, we have a>b>c.

problems.title: Minimum over the sine range
problems.question: Minimize sin²x−4sinx+7.
problems.idea: Use trigonometric identities and a perpendicular-section or vector model for spatial geometry.
formulas: Put t=sinx∈[−1,1]. The expression is(t−2)²+3.
steps: The closest permitted t to 2 is 1, giving minimum 4.

problems.title: A full increasing interval of sine
problems.question: Which listed interval is an interval of increase of sinx?
problems.idea: Use trigonometric identities and a perpendicular-section or vector model for spatial geometry.
formulas: Sine increases on(−π/2+2kπ,π/2+2kπ).
steps: Take k=2 to obtain(7π/2,9π/2), the listed interval. The other choices include decreasing portions.

problems.title: Common perpendicular of skew lines
problems.question: How many segments join two skew lines and are perpendicular to both?
problems.idea: Use trigonometric identities and a perpendicular-section or vector model for spatial geometry.
formulas: Two skew lines have a unique common perpendicular.
steps: Its two feet lie on the respective lines, so exactly 1 such segment exists.

problems.title: Ratio of two sector areas
problems.question: Compare a120° sector of radius 2R with aπ/3-radian sector of radius R.
problems.idea: Use trigonometric identities and a perpendicular-section or vector model for spatial geometry.
formulas: Sector are a=θr²/2, with θ in radians. The angle ratio is(2π/3)/(π/3)=2, and squared-radius ratio4.
steps: The are a ratio is 2·4=8.

problems.title: Double-angle cosine from tangent
problems.question: Find cos2α if tanα=2.
problems.idea: Use trigonometric identities and a perpendicular-section or vector model for spatial geometry.
formulas: cos2α=(1−tan²α)/(1+tan²α).

problems.title: A half-angle condition and quadrant conventions
problems.question: y=−3+xcos(α/2) is increasing. In which quadrants can α lie?
problems.idea: Use trigonometric identities and a perpendicular-section or vector model for spatial geometry.
formulas: The slope condition is cos(α/2)>0. With unrestricted real angles, it is not invariant under replacing α by α+2π.
steps: Angles α=π/3,2π/3,−2π/3,−π/3 satisfy the condition and have terminal sides in quadrants I, II, III, IV, respectively.
Thus all 4 quadrants are possible as printed.
problems.note: If an unstated convention0<α<2π were imposed, only quadrants I and II would work. The source does not give that angle range.

problems.title: Count even functions
problems.question: Among sin³x, cos5x, x⁶(x+4), cos⁵x,|5x|,|tanx+sinx|, how many are even?
problems.idea: Use trigonometric identities and a perpendicular-section or vector model for spatial geometry.
formulas: Cosine is even; odd-function absolute values are even on symmetric domains.
steps: The even functions are cos5x, cos⁵x,|5x|, and|tanx+sinx|. The first sine cube is odd, and x⁶(x+4) contains an odd x⁷ term.

problems.title: Line-plane inclination versus another in-plane line
problems.question: An oblique line makes45° with a plane. A line through its foot makes45° with its projection. Find the angle between the lines.
problems.idea: Use trigonometric identities and a perpendicular-section or vector model for spatial geometry.
formulas: The cosine of the line angle is cos(inclination)·cos(projection angle).
steps: Thus cosθ=cos45°cos45°=1/2, so θ=60°.

problems.title: Planes through one of two parallel lines
problems.question: How many planes through line a are parallel to a distinct parallel line b?
problems.idea: Use trigonometric identities and a perpendicular-section or vector model for spatial geometry.
formulas: Infinitely many planes pass through a. Only one contains b as well.
steps: Every other such plane is disjoint from b, so is parallel to b. There are infinitely many choices.

problems.title: Reduce shifted trigonometric arguments
problems.question: At α=π/3, evaluate sin²(α/2+7π/2)+cos²(α/2−9π/2)+tan²(α/2+5π/2)+sin(3π/2−α)/[1+cos(π−α)].
problems.idea: Use trigonometric identities and a perpendicular-section or vector model for spatial geometry.
formulas: The four terms are 3/4,1/4,3, and −1, respectively.
steps: The first two sum 1. Adding3 and −1 gives 3.

problems.title: Period of a cosine-tangent sum
problems.question: Find the least positive period of cosx+tan2x.
problems.idea: Use trigonometric identities and a perpendicular-section or vector model for spatial geometry.
formulas: Cosx has period2π; tan2x has periodπ/2. A common period is 2π.
steps: The tangent poles force any period to be an integer multiple of π/2. Its tangent part then repeats exactly, and the cosine term repeats only at multiples of 2π.

problems.title: Tangent sum from tangent and cotangent sums
problems.question: tanα+tanβ=2, cotα+cotβ=3. Find tan(α+β).
problems.idea: Use trigonometric identities and a perpendicular-section or vector model for spatial geometry.
formulas: Let p=tanαtanβ. The cotangent sum is 2/p=3, so p=2/3.

problems.title: Sine addition with acute angles
problems.question: sinα=1/5, sinβ=1/3, with both angles in(0,π/4). Find sin(α+β).
problems.idea: Use trigonometric identities and a perpendicular-section or vector model for spatial geometry.
steps: Use sin(α+β)=sinαcosβ+cosαsinβ=(2√2+2√6)/15.

problems.title: Point equidistant from square vertices
problems.question: A point S is 7 cm from every vertex of a square side 6 in planeα. Find its distance to the plane.
problems.idea: Use trigonometric identities and a perpendicular-section or vector model for spatial geometry.
formulas: The perpendicular foot is the square centre, whose vertex distance is 6/√2=3√2.
steps: By Pythagoras, h²+18=49, so h=√31 cm.

problems.title: Distances to two perpendicular axes
problems.question: A point outside a right-angle plane is 5 from the vertex and 4 from each side line. Find its distance to the plane.
problems.idea: Use trigonometric identities and a perpendicular-section or vector model for spatial geometry.
formulas: Use coordinates M=(x, y, h), with side lines the x- and y-axes. Then x²+y²+h²=25, x²+h²=16, y²+h²=16.
steps: Add the last two and subtract the first:h²=32−25=7.

problems.title: One zero factor is enough
problems.question: Evaluate sin(1!°)sin(2!°)…sin(45!°).
problems.idea: Use trigonometric identities and a perpendicular-section or vector model for spatial geometry.
steps: The product contains this zero factor, so it is 0.

problems.title: A horizontal line above a parabola minimum
problems.question: Count intersections of y=x²+(sin199°)x+sin199° and y=sin10°sin20°sin40°sin80°.
problems.idea: Use trigonometric identities and a perpendicular-section or vector model for spatial geometry.
formulas: s=sin199°<0, so the parabola’s minimum s−s²/4 is negative. The horizontal constant is positive because all 4 sine factors are positive.
steps: A horizontal line strictly above an upward parabola’s minimum meets it in2 points.

problems.title: Maximum of a triple trigonometric sum
problems.question: Maximize sinx siny sinz+cosx cosy cosz.
problems.idea: Use trigonometric identities and a perpendicular-section or vector model for spatial geometry.
formulas: For fixed y, z, Cauchy–Schwarz bounds the expression by √(sin²y sin²z+cos²y cos²z)≤√(sin²y+cos²y)=1.
steps: Equality is attained at x=y=z=0. Thus the maximum is 1.

problems.title: Inclination of a square diagonal
problems.question: Two parallel planes are 4√2 apart. A square side 8 has adjacent vertices A, B on one plane and C, D on the other. Find the angle between AC and the second plane.
problems.idea: Use trigonometric identities and a perpendicular-section or vector model for spatial geometry.
formulas: AC=8√2, and its perpendicular component across the planes is 4√2.

problems.title: Signed distance of a division point
problems.question: AB crosses a plane, with endpoint distances10,22. K divides AK:KB=1:3. Find K’s distance.
problems.idea: Use trigonometric identities and a perpendicular-section or vector model for spatial geometry.
formulas: Assign signed distances10,−22. A point one quarter of the way from A to B has signed distance(3·10−22)/4=2.
steps: Its ordinary distance is|2|=2.

problems.title: A cubic with a floored-sine constant
problems.question: Which listed α makes√(floor(sinα))=4x³−πx have 3 distinct roots?
problems.idea: Use trigonometric identities and a perpendicular-section or vector model for spatial geometry.
formulas: For α=7π/3, sinα=√3/2, so floor(sinα)=0.
steps: The equation becomes x(4x²−π)=0, with roots 0,±√π/2. Every other listed α has negative sine, so its floored value is −1 and the real square root is undefined.

problems.title: Minimum of sixth and double-angle powers
problems.question: Minimize sin⁶x+cos²2x+cos⁶x.
problems.idea: Use trigonometric identities and a perpendicular-section or vector model for spatial geometry.
formulas: Let t=sin²xcos²x∈[0,1/4]. Then sin⁶x+cos⁶x=1−3t and cos²2x=1−4t.
steps: The sum is 2−7t, minimized at t=1/4. Its minimum is 1/4.

problems.title: Parallel-line distances from an external point
problems.question: A point is 5,6 from two parallel lines, and 3 from their plane. Which listed line separation is possible?
problems.idea: Use trigonometric identities and a perpendicular-section or vector model for spatial geometry.
formulas: The point’s projection into their plane is √(25−9)=4 from one line and √(36−9)=3√3 from the other.
steps: The line separation is either4+3√3 or|4−3√3|. Only the first is listed.

problems.title: Midpoint distance bound on skew lines
problems.question: E, F are midpoints of segments AB, CD on skew lines. Which listed inequality always holds?
problems.idea: Use trigonometric identities and a perpendicular-section or vector model for spatial geometry.
formulas: Vector EF=(AD+BC)/2. The triangle inequality gives|AD+BC|≤|AD|+|BC|.
steps: Hence EF≤(AD+BC)/2, where the right-hand lengths are ordinary segment lengths.
